name: Candidate-State Personalization & Trajectory Divergence
research_question: Does candidate-state-driven personalization produce measurably different and more targeted interview trajectories than non-adaptive questioning?
hypothesis: Personalization actively diverges question difficulty and topic remediation based on measured candidate state, avoiding topic starvation and question repetition, while non-adaptive random selection fails to remediate weaknesses.

selection_modes.name: Uniform Random Non-Adaptive Selection
selection_modes.description: Selects questions uniformly at random from the 125-question bank without tracking candidate state, weaknesses, or difficulty targets.

selection_modes.name: Baseline Topic-Count Question Selector
selection_modes.description: Selects questions using topic-frequency balancing and nearest difficulty match without candidate state adaptation.

selection_modes.name: Production Candidate-State Adaptive Selector
selection_modes.description: Production selector utilizing 3-level deduplication (ID, text, Jaccard overlap >= 0.75), difficulty <= 2 Easy-start guarantee, weakness remediation, and strength advancement.
